the CARRY located every work item correctly but described two of them wrongly, caught only by reading source: the preflight.rs:335 family is a retry last-attempt guard (poll_canary computes no deadline at all) not poll-deadline arithmetic, which changes the killing shape from an outcome assertion to a timing one; and the prescribed per-test temp obs sink is ALREADY present in the failing test, so the real cause is the process-global subscriber (first-install-wins) plus an unsafe RUST_LOG set_var, not the sink path. Both descriptors were transcribed from the audit proposals text one step earlier in this same session, so the phrasing propagated author-to-author without anyone reading the code

the tests distiller found cargo-mutants registered nowhere in test-plan (§4 tool inventory and floors policy, §9 pipeline stages, §10 gates, §12 decisions log all silent), so the chunk operator-set acceptance instrument — a scoped mutation re-run with --test-tool=nextest and stub_pulse_mcp excluded — is an out-of-plan tool; whether it becomes a standing gate is a wrap-time plan-amendment question the extract correctly declined to assume

the obs extract asserted that obs-plan §4 cli row requires manual #[tracing::instrument] on fn main() and core scenario handlers, which would have made the unused-tracing rider a spec breach and forced an operator fork; grepping obs-plan showed the cli row (:48) names only the tracing crate plus a tracing-subscriber JSON formatter, and every #[tracing::instrument] mandate sits on the desktop-webview (:49) and ipc-internal (:50) rows about #[tauri::command] handlers — a mis-citation onto a different surface, not an absence, and conductor-cli satisfies its actual row through conductor_core::init_observability at main.rs:28

research carried the right file list and closed all three premises but never enumerated the survivor families from the authoritative c-mutation-*.json, inheriting the counts from the scope table instead; synthesis needed four extra reads (declares enclosing fn, conductor-run public surface, the audit mutation command, the full survivor lists) and the JSON then corrected declares 5 to 6 and MAX_LINE_BYTES 3 to 5 — the latter changing the test design, since only an at-limit-accepted case kills the two constant-expression mutants

research and the plan named crates/conductor-run/tests/* and a new tests/jsonrpc_line_bound.rs as the homes for all five killing-test families, but visibility decides reachability and was never checked: JsonRpcSession is pub(crate) (reachable only because ReadbackClient::connect_transport happens to be pub), while declares/observe_run_contract and execute_scenario are reachable only in-crate because Preflight has no public constructor — lib.rs already carries a blocked_preflight() helper and four execute_scenario/drive_run tests inside its own cfg(test) module for exactly that reason

the paused-clock step could not compile until conductor-verify gained tokio test-util in dev-dependencies; neither plan nor research named it, and the convention was recovered by reading the two crates that already use start_paused (conductor-run and conductor-core both list test-util in their dev-dependency feature sets)

The tests extract faithfully reported test-plan 5/8 as mandating the MCP sidecar be exercised through an injected rmcp stub transport, while the arch extract reported the 2026-06-27 decision REVERSAL that removed rmcp entirely for a hand-rolled JSON-RPC client. The distiller was correct to state its plan mandate; the spec source names a mechanism that no longer exists. Already owned by the Epoch-5 working-route entry whose text says with the stale rmcp wording reconciled, so not newly deferred and not fixable here (phase is read-only on specs).

Plan step 2 specified the budget-vs-tier invariant as a #[garde(custom(...))] on Scenario::expected, but garde 0.22.1's field-level custom receives only (&field, &()) and cannot see the sibling slo_tier field, so the rule structurally cannot be a garde validator; shipped instead as Scenario::check_budgets() called from from_toml_str, the exact shape of its structural sibling check_capabilities

Two conventions the plan and research did not state had to be read from neighbouring code: CoreError::Validation is #[from] garde::Report and cannot carry a hand-written message (so the budget fault uses CoreError::Config, matching check_capabilities), and conductor-report does not depend on serde directly, so a generic wire_as_value helper would not compile and the three enum conversions were inlined the way into_record already does it

A canonical IMPACT query on calls for effective_deadline_ms returned 0 rows at db_state fresh; the cookbook-prescribed Q4 re-probe CONFIRMED the symbol is indexed, which by the cookbook makes 0 rows a real leaf finding — but a grep cross-check found a genuine production caller at conductor-verify/src/slo.rs:84 inside evaluate_check. The calls edge is simply absent from a fresh rust-plane DB. The cookbook reading protocol names only two cases (confirmed-indexed = real finding, or index gap = symbol absent) and has no third case for symbol-indexed-but-edge-missing, so following it exactly would have yielded a false leaf conclusion on the very symbol this chunk turns on.

Both the working entry and the v2-29 matrix acceptance say the count freezes without naming a surface; the answer (the CLI suite spinner, since commands/run.rs passes spinner None and only commands/suite.rs passes Some) came from a codebase trace during scope expansion rather than from either stated artifact.

a11y and tests pull opposite ways on the webview checklist surface and P2 aggregate check C did not catch it: a11y-plan names the operator-checklist a must-be-accessible path with a mandated shape, while test-plan §5 defers the webview render leg to the Epoch-9 tauri-driver chunk and the axe/wdio harness is display-gated to Linux+xvfb, so it cannot run on this host. Not a content contradiction but an ownership/scheduling one, invisible to a reciprocity check because each extract is internally consistent. Resolved at synthesis by separating the claim from the verification: v2-29 method is manual, so the operator confirms the render and no WCAG conformance is claimed, leaving the machine a11y verification owed exactly as it already was.
